newsitem.title: FRANCE: French shares fall sharply after Wall Street slide.
newsitem.headline: French shares fall sharply after Wall Street slide.

text.p: French shares started the New Year with big losses in early trade on Thursday on the back of the Dow Jones industrial average's 101-point tumble on Tuesday.
The French market's slide was greased by thin post-holiday volume. Othe European bourses also showed big falls.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index opened down 0.43 percent and by mid-morning was 1.72 percent or 40.09 points lower at 2,275.64 at 1012 GMT, just above its intraday low of 2,273.39.
The CAC-40 futures contract was down 38 points at 2,278.0. by thin post-holiday trade. Volume totalled 584 million francs by 0932 GMT. Other European bourses also showed big falls.
The Dow's slide was triggered by a batch of economic data showing strong economic growth, raising fears of interest rate tightening to curb inflation.

"We're basically following Wall Street," a bourse trader said. He said the market was waiting for U.S. jobless claims due at 1330 GMT and data from the National Association of Purchasing Managers. He said the biggest losers among the CAC-40 shares were primarily those that had gained the most recently.

All the CAC-40 constituent stocks were marked lower, aside from Eurotunnel, up 0.73 percent at 6.90 francs retracing some of its nearly three percent drop on Tuesday after one of its trains was stranded in the Channel Tunnel by an engine failure.

Among the biggest losers were leisure group Accor, down 3.04 percent at 637 francs, sugar company Eridania Beghin-Say 2.28 percent weaker at 816 francs and drugs firm Rhone Poulenc, off 2.71 percent at 172.10.
The car sector also continued to show weakness with Renault 2.60 percent lower at 108.60 francs, and PSA Peugeot Citroen down 2.91 percent at 567 francs.

Temporary help firm Bis remained suspended at 533 francs after last weekend's death of company chairman Laurent Negro. Bis has appointed board member Claude Charbonniaud to succeed Negro. His death has rewewed speculation Bis could be the target of a takeover bid by a large foreign employment firm.
